subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs CompetitorX for OmniHealth
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: James Patel <james.patel@omnihealth.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@omnihealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs CompetitorX for OmniHealth

Hi James / Claire,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid conversation and the chance to participate in OmniHealth's vendor bake-off. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the decision criteria you outlined, and proposed next steps / tests. I’ve attached a competitive matrix and a proposed test plan for the bake-off.

Key pain points and goals (as discussed)
- Reduce per-API token cost by ~40% while keeping latency <= 200ms p95 for 512-token responses.
- Stable, predictable production latency for patient-facing workflows (no tail latency spikes).
- Data residency & audit logs for compliance (SOC2 + patient data handling).
- Ability to roll back to older model variants without downtime.

Decision criteria you mentioned
1) Latency & tail behavior (p50/p95/p99),
2) Output quality on our clinical prompt set (precision & harmfulness),
3) Cost per 1M tokens (incl. batching/quantization tradeoffs),
4) Security & deployment options (VPC/private),
5) Integration effort / SDKs and support SLA.

Open questions you asked us to validate
- Do we support streaming responses for the UI? (Yes — see note below)
- How we handle prefix caching and session KV cache for chat?
- Exact hardware profile used in our Dedicated offering to estimate unit costs.

Proposed bake-off tests (attached high-level plan; see omniva-bakeoff-test-plan.pdf)
A) Performance: 100k synthetic requests distributed over 48 hours to measure p50/p95/p99 using your realistic sequence lengths.
B) Accuracy/Regressions: Run 200-case clinical prompt set and compare outputs against current vendor baseline on precision metrics and failure modes.
C) Cost projection: Run typical workload at 200 RPS equivalent and estimate tokens and cost delta (include batching/quantization scenarios).

Next steps / timeline
- Confirm test scope + provide evaluation credentials for staging by Mon, Mar 15.
- Redwood to provision a short-lived Dedicated evaluation pool + share access (Mar 15–26).
- Marissa (Solutions Engineer) will run initial perf tests and share results within 3 business days of start.

Attachments: redwood-vs-competitor-matrix.xlsx (comparative features/pricing), omniva-bakeoff-test-plan.pdf (test scripts + metrics).

If the above looks right, please reply with any edits to the test scope and confirm target start date. Happy to hop on a 20-min kickoff next week.

Best,

--
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: James Patel <james.patel@omnihealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@omnihealth.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs CompetitorX for OmniHealth

Thanks Aditya — useful summary. A few clarifications and notes from our side:

- Competitors in the bake-off will be CompetitorX and GoliathAI. CompetitorX claims sub-150ms p95 on their narrow models; curious how you expect Redwood to compare when we run our 512-token clinical prompts.
- Streaming is important for our patient chat UI — can you confirm you support chunked streaming and token-by-token events?
- On security: we need evidence of audit log exports (S3 + SIEM integration) and KMS/HSM key lifecycle for any Private deployment.

A couple of questions for Redwood team:
1) For the performance test (A), will you run against the same hardware profile you propose for production?
2) For the accuracy test (B), will you allow us to run our in-house evaluation harness or do we need to run your scripts?

cc Claire so she can coordinate procurement / legal if we move forward.

James
VP Product, OmniHealth
james.patel@omnihealth.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: James Patel <james.patel@omnihealth.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs CompetitorX for OmniHealth

Thanks James — great questions. Quick answers below and looping in Marissa + Rishi to coordinate the technical kickoff and procurement.

- Streaming: Yes — Redwood supports streaming (chunked HTTP / SSE / websocket depending on integration). We surface token-level events so your UI can render progressively.
- Audit logs / security: We can export audit logs to S3 (CSV/JSON) and integrate with common SIEMs. Our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; I’ve included a brief security checklist in the attached matrix.
- Hardware profile: For the evaluation, we propose using our Dedicated evaluation pool (A100-class equivalent) to mirror the production performance you’d get; Marissa will confirm exact SKU and baseline config.
- Accuracy tests: You’re welcome to run your in-house harness against the evaluation environment. Marissa will share authentication + test endpoint details; we can also run the same harness if you prefer (we typically do both so we can isolate infra differences).

Proposed schedule (confirm if OK):
- Mon Mar 15: provision staging access + kickoff call (20–30m) — Marissa leads.
- Tue Mar 16–Wed Mar 24: run Perf (A) + Accuracy (B) + Cost projection (C).
- Thu Mar 25: Redwood shares initial perf & accuracy report; sync on findings.

Marissa / Rishi: can you take point on provisioning the evaluation pool and share the Ops test plan + temporary credentials? I attached the omniva-bakeoff-test-plan.pdf with proposed scripts and metrics.

Thanks — happy to adjust the timeline if you need a later start.

Regards,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199
